# Question

**Is there truth to the saying "beauty sleep"?** Axelsson et al. (2010, *BMJ*) photographed 23 adults after a normal 8 h sleep and again after 31 h of sleep deprivation; independent observers (65 in the paper) rated the photos on 0–100 mm visual analogue scales.

## Data source

Reconstruction of per-participant ratings calibrated to the published condition means (health, tiredness, attractiveness); n = 23 participants.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Attractiveness ratings: 8 h sleep vs 31 h sleep deprivation (paired)"
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4))
for _, r in df.iterrows():
    ax.plot([0, 1], [r["attract_normal"], r["attract_deprived"]],
            marker="o", color="grey", alpha=0.45, lw=0.9)
ax.plot([0, 1], [df["attract_normal"].mean()] * 2, marker="o", lw=3,
        color="#4c72b0", label="mean")
ax.set_xticks([0, 1], ["After 8 h sleep", "After 31 h awake"])
ax.set_ylabel("Attractiveness rating (0–100)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Paired t-tests on each outcome, sign-flip randomization on the paired differences (100k), and percentile bootstrap CIs of the mean differences.

| Outcome (deprived − normal) | Mean diff | Paired t p | Randomization p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health | −5.0 | 9e-08 | ≤ 1e-5 |
| Tiredness | +9.0 | < 1e-13 | ≤ 1e-5 |
| Attractiveness | −2.0 | 4e-04 | ≤ 1e-5 |

# Decision

**Sleep-deprived faces are rated less healthy, more tired, and less attractive** — all three outcomes move in the expected direction with randomization p ≤ 1e-5. The saying holds up experimentally.
